proposals.proposed_tex:
Let $B\ge2$ be the integer window parameter, let
$I\subset[-B,B]\cap\mathbb Z$ have positive even cardinality $m$,
and let $x$ be a positive integer. If $x>(B+1)^{5m}$, then
$\prod_{a\in I}(x+a)$ is not an integer square.
proposals.proposed_proof_tex:
The threshold implies $x\ge2B$. If the product were a square,
Lemma~\ref{p1:arith:runge}, with $R=B$ and $d=m$, would give
$x\le(64B)^m\le(B+1)^{5m}$, a contradiction.

proposals.proposed_tex:
Fix integers $r\ge s\ge2$. For $r$ logarithmic blocks with
distinct centres in the height and width regime of
Theorem~\ref{p13:half:conditional}, the number of tuples admitting
a relation whose effective projection is nonzero in at least $s$
blocks is
\[
 O_{r,C,D,\varepsilon}\bigl(N^{r-s/2+\varepsilon}\bigr).
\]
Here each block space is the image of its even selections in the
square-class space; the selection map need not be injective.
The same estimate allows $B^{O_r(1)}$ offset and motif choices with
fixed width and dilation bounds. All these parameters are fixed
before the scale threshold.
proposals.proposed_proof_tex:
Choose $s$ nonzero effective projections and fix the other
$r-s$ centres. The chosen projections sum into the full value span
of these fixed blocks, so Theorem~\ref{p13:half:conditional} gives
$O(N^{s/2+\varepsilon'})$ choices. Summing over the complement and
the finitely many choices of blocks gives
$O(N^{r-s/2+\varepsilon'})$. Reduce $\varepsilon'$ to absorb the
polynomial number of offset and motif choices. Every nonzero
effective vector has a nonempty even-selection representative;
no injectivity of the selection map is required.

separate_option.proposed_bridge_tex:
The argument also bounds separated homogeneous triples in the
regular set $G_N$ which are connected and contain a pair in the
raw geometric good-edge family, in either channel $2:3$ or $3:4$.
Writing $q_0(T)=2^{-\dim(\sum_{x\in T}S_x)}$, one has
\[
 \sum_T q_0(T)\ll_{C,\varepsilon}N^{-41/30+\varepsilon}.
\]
Indeed, use $q_0(e)\le N^{-\kappa_b+o(1)}$ and the exact marginal
$q_0(\{z\})=p$ in the nonaligned sector. The aligned-sector argument
is a rank estimate on the merged true values. When two physical
coefficients agree, the imposed separation $|x-y|\ge L$ replaces
the use of affine compatibility; equality at $L$ remains allowed.
Thus incompatible affine prescriptions are included in this
homogeneous sum.
separate_option.proposed_T4_4_proof_tex:
For one target, a raw good pair has nonzero relative dependence,
and a positive crossing with the target makes their union a
connected triple. Apply the homogeneous estimate following the
proof of Proposition~\ref{p13:third:aligned-family}. Each triple
has at most three choices of its marked source pair, so the total
mass is $O(N^{-41/30+\varepsilon})$ in either channel. Original
affine joint probabilities are bounded by the same homogeneous
probabilities.
